evidence: Cic. Sen. 46: quae mihi sermōnis aviditātem auxit
Liv. 21.33.6: quōs nemora etiam repercussaeque vallēs augēbant
terms.comment: Transitive; in the passive, “to increase, grow”.

evidence: Liv. 3.26.4: crēvit ex metū aliēnō, ut fit, audācia
terms.comment: Of what grows or increases by itself.

evidence: Cic. Sen. 52: vītium ortūs, satūs, incrēmenta
Ov. Rem. 98: plūrima collēctīs multiplicantur aquīs
terms.comment: Of what grows many times over, as a river does by gathering streams; in arithmetic, to multiply (see multiply).

terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation, with the accusative
evidence: Cic. Or. 113: manum, opposite comprimere digitōs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Make larger in extent, spread out: a camp, the open hand, a line of battle, and figuratively a speech or a name (“especially frequent in Cicero”, Lewis & Short). In the Moretum it is flattening dough into a round (palmīsque suum dīlātat in orbem, Mor. 48).

phrases.latin: habeōque senectūtī magnam grātiam, quae mihi sermōnis aviditātem auxit, pōtiōnis et cibī sustulit
phrases.english: and I am very grateful to old age, which has increased my appetite for conversation and taken away my appetite for food and drink

phrases.latin: crēvit ex metū aliēnō, ut fit, audācia
phrases.english: as usually happens, their boldness grew with the other side’s fear

phrases.latin: flūmina pauca vidēs dē magnīs fontibus orta: plūrima collēctīs multiplicantur aquīs
phrases.english: few rivers, you see, rise from great springs; most grow by gathering waters
